items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Ray Sherman was born in Chicago in 1923 but has been an integral part of the west coast music scene for many years. His first exposure came in L.A. in 1939 and he gained valuable experience in the Army with Ray Bauduc and Gil Rodin.

ctx.x: Was it at that time, when you were going in the service, was it a question of I’m going overseas?

Well it’s funny I don’t know, in those days people, I don’t know, they weren’t as sensitive about it, maybe it’s since the Vietnam thing. Like if you could work deals, you know, nobody put you down. If you had connections where you could stay in the country for the duration or whatever, I mean it was fine, go do it. And my dad knew Gil Rodin, you are familiar with him? And he was up in Vallejo with Ray Bauduc, they were both in the same group up there. And I don’t know how my dad knew that, but he contacted Gil…

happened to come to the base, you know, oh, there’s a piano player. I mean you had to get them from someplace. So Gil said he’d see what he could do to get me up there. Because they did need a piano player.
